questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Area of the Image of an Object Under a Linear Transformation Given a Diagram
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14014125/assets/fa0dbfe03050a0ca52f2fbe1988a9e6475cd24437c619dba27a4fed984736fc1.png)

Consider the shaded region $D$ shown above. What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that for any linear transformation $T,$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $T(D)$ under the action of $T:$

$$
\text{Area}(T(D))=|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot 6=9.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
det(T)=3\cdot 4-2\cdot 2=8.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,8\,|\cdot 9 \\  & =72.\end{aligned}
$$
